A recorded computer experiment

In the reported computer experiment, slower movement reduces one kind of error but allows more of the signal to fade away. The best overall return among the four tested settings occurs at an intermediate speed.

Choose a setting and compare both numbers. These are saved results from that computer model. They are not measurements from a physical device or a best setting for every device.

Choose a setting. A larger number means a slower loop here. Compare how much signal returns with how much is lost.

Words used here
model
A simplified description used to explore a question. A result in the model needs further evidence before it describes the real world.
Read the fuller explanation

The documented four-mode numerical experiment compares several loop rates. In its metered example, slowing the loop suppresses bright leakage while accumulated dissipation rises. The raw target overlap peaks at one of the tested intermediate rates.

The rate cards show reported values from that software record. They are not new browser measurements or a universal optimum for real devices. A survival-conditioned view and the raw return answer different questions; the lost part must not disappear from the account.

The wider frontier asks for work, heat, precision, preparation, sampling and verification costs as well as a desired state. What would count as success if every impressive result quietly discarded its expense?
